function: Learned (DDPG) hybrid RIS phase and amplitude configuration under a fixed zero-forcing precoder, maximising a fairness-regularised sum secrecy rate against one eavesdropper (pp. 5-7)
system: MU-MISO downlink: 8-antenna BS, 4 single-antenna users, one passive eavesdropper, hybrid RIS (half active, half passive reflecting elements), 2.4 GHz, Rayleigh fading (pp. 3-4, 8)
method: DDPG actor-critic reinforcement learning (off-policy, replay buffer, OU exploration, soft target updates), trained over 10,000 episodes of 100 steps on Rayleigh channels (pp. 6-8)
data_channel: Custom simulator: i.i.d. Rayleigh fading on all links, path-loss exponent 3.2, fixed node distances; new channels drawn each episode; no standardized model or dataset (pp. 4, 7-8)
test_conditions: Random Rayleigh draws for training and testing, same geometry; RIS size and power vary in separate training curves; generalization to new users or sizes claimed, not tested (pp. 8-11)
baselines: Classical: alternating optimisation (AO/BCD) method of [52] (Fig. 11); passive and active RIS variants under the same DDPG; no other learned method compared (pp. 9, 11-12)
metrics: Average sum secrecy rate and average sum user rate (bps/Hz) versus transmit power, RIS size and training steps; empirical CDF of the optimal user rate (pp. 9-11)
complexity: Per-iteration O(Nb (ds+da) Nhidden); online inference one actor forward pass, O((ds+da) Nhidden); no runtime or FLOP measurements (pp. 3, 8)
openness: none; parameters listed in Table 2, no code or data link
q1_support: p. 4: "A Rayleigh fading channel model is considered where all the links are assumed to be independent and identically distributed"; custom simulator with distance path loss, no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 8: "Rayleigh channels are emulated, preventing overfitting to a single topology"; fresh draws of the same distribution and geometry, and the claimed adaptation to new users or RIS sizes (p. 8) is not tested.
q3_support: p. 11: "compared with the conventional alternating optimization (AO/BCD)-based method adopted in [52]"; no earlier learned method is compared, and the active and passive RIS curves are variants of the same DDPG.
q4_support: p. 8: "per-iteration complexity is on the order of O(Nb (ds + da )Nhidden )"; online inference is a single actor forward pass (p. 3).
q5_support: p. 8: "to improve clarity and reproducibility"; Table 2 lists the parameters, but there is no code or data link and no public dataset, since the channels come from the paper's own Rayleigh simulator.
notes: Included as area 3: the learned function is the hybrid RIS configuration (phases and amplitudes) with a fixed ZF precoder, even though the goal is secrecy. Fig. 11 compares only with the AO/BCD method of [52] (non-learned); there is no learned baseline, so q3=0. Table 2 gives L=30 while the figures use L in {4, 8, 16, 32}. The claim of generalizing to new users or RIS sizes (p. 8) has no experiment; q4 rests on the stated order of complexity only.
